title.narrative: Reviving Roots: Economic and Community Recovery for Sustainable Return

description.narrative: ltpgtAleppo city, once Syria’s industrial and cultural heart, continues to heal from the effects of prolonged conflict. Despite increasing return movements, returnees and host communities face overlapping challenges: destroyed infrastructure, widespread unemployment, and a near-collapse of local economic systems. The shortage of skilled labor, particularly among youth and returnees, further limits recovery, even where political and security conditions permit return.ltbrgtThis project aims to facilitate sustainable return and reintegration in Aleppo city by restoring access to livelihoods and community services through inclusive, locally led recovery. It addresses three intersecting needs: unemployment, damaged infrastructure, and small business recovery. The project adopts a dual approach, targeting both returnees and host communities, in line with the Syrian Humanitarian Fund (SHF) 2025 First Standard Allocation Strategy under Envelope 2.ltbrgtThe first component focuses on job creation through light rehabilitation of markets and public spaces. Sixty engineers from returnee and host communities, with a focus on youth and women, will be trained in damage assessments, rehabilitation cost evaluations, and conflict-sensitive rehabilitation planning. These engineers will then conduct detailed assessments of 600 shops and 15 public infrastructure assets in Dahret Awwad, Hanano, and the Old City. Based on criteria developed with the Aleppo Chamber of Commerce, 100 shops will be selected for rehabilitation along with 8 public spaces. Thirty engineers and 60 skilled laborers will be contracted to carry out the works, creating immediate job opportunities while restoring essential community and commercial infrastructure.ltbrgtThe second component supports microeconomic revitalization. Following rehabilitation, 45 shop owners will receive small grants to restart their businesses, ensuring that restored spaces quickly translate into renewed economic activity. This combination of physical rehabilitation and targeted financial support will help stabilize livelihoods, foster market recovery, and improve access to services for both returnees and host communities.ltbrgtThe project also builds long-term local capacity. By training and contracting engineers and skilled laborers from Aleppo, it creates a pool of professionals with market-relevant skills that will continue to benefit the city’s recovery well beyond the project timeline. At the same time, by involving both returnees and host communities in shared activities, it strengthens social cohesion and trust.ltbrgtThis project complements prior interventions carried out by the foundation. Sanad brings strong experience in livelihoods and early recovery programming. Under the 2024 SHF Standard Allocation in Rural Damascus (Qudsaya), Sanad trained 300 youth in soft skills, provided vocational and technical training to 150 individuals, supported 50 new startups and 30 existing MSMEs with grants, and facilitated on-the-job training to enhance employability. Sanad also partnered with the Aga Khan Foundation to support 15 tech-based MSMEs and with the ILO to provide job training for over 150 youth. This proven model of skills development, business support, and employment creation informs the proposed intervention in Aleppo’s return-affected communities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
